newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI credit return flow hit by slowdown.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI credit return flow hit by slowdown.

text.p: The country's largest commercial bank State Bank of India (SBI) said on Thursday the percentage of net non performing assets (NPA) to net advances rose in the financial year ended March 31.

"The percentage of net NPA to net advances stood at 7.3 percent at end-March 1997, recording a 0.7 percentage point increase over the corresponding percentage at end March 1996," the bank said in a statement.
SBI said this was mainly due to a slowdown in economic activity, particularly in the second half of 1996/97, which adversely affected the return flow of credit.
"This is also due to less than proportionate credit offtake during the year," SBI said.
The bank said its domestic investments grew by 6.5 percent to reach a level of 467.12 billion rupees by the end of March.

"The bulk of investments was in government and other approved securities (90.7 percent), followed by investments in shares, debentures and bonds (7.4 percent) and investments in associates and subsidiaries (1.9 percent)," SBI said.

"Working towards internationally accepted accounting standards, the bank marked to market 70.9 percent of its SLR (statutory liquidity ratio) investments, well above the Reserve Bank norm of 50 percent," the bank added.
